name: Aleksei Solberg
role: Street pharmacist and herbal remedy vendor
location: The Alban Souk, permanent pitch near the eastern water cisterns, near Pulaski and Chicago Ave
description:
Aleksei Solberg is a broad-shouldered woman with dark amber skin weathered by decades of outdoor market life, her natural hair tucked under a wide-brimmed plastene hat strung with dried medicinal herbs and small glass vials. Her eyes are warm brown with cosmetic irises that shift between a deep violet and copper-gold depending on the light — a cheap mod she got thirty years ago that she's never bothered to remove. Her hands are her most striking feature: enormous, steady, and perpetually stained with pigment from the botanical pastes she grinds fresh every morning.

She occupies a peculiar moral middle ground in the Souk — selling everything from genuine herbal supplements and unlicensed over-the-counter analogs to mild synth-narcotics she insists are 'medicinal.' She's not cruel, but she's not naive either. She mothers the young addicts who come to her while simultaneously keeping them coming back, a contradiction she rarely examines. Her stall is famous for a handwritten sign that reads: 'No judgment. No refunds. Ancestors watching.' She burns incense for the local E.L.F. that she calls Mama Cistern every morning before opening.

core_fears: Dying having caused more harm than good
Being exposed as complicit in someone's overdose death
core_desires: To be genuinely needed, not just useful
To open a proper licensed clinic before she dies
coping_mechanisms: Ritual — morning incense and prayer to Mama Cistern
blind_spots: She rationalizes enabling addiction as harm reduction
She underestimates how much people depend on her as an emotional anchor
psychology.secret: Three years ago a teenage boy named Pires Fonseca-Amadi died of a compound interaction from two things she sold him separately. She told no one, scattered his ashes into the cisterns herself, and has silently funded his younger sister's school fees ever since through an anonymous Guild charity account.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Warm, maternal, medicalized slang mixed with old Igbo endearments and Polish curses; uses plant names as metaphors
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and deliberate, like she's measuring every word the way she measures doses
example_lines: 'My dear, what you have is not a headache. What you have is a debt your body is collecting on. Sit.'
'I sell remedies, not miracles. If you want miracles, the E.L.F. shrine is three stalls east. But she charges more than I do.'

story_hooks: A bad batch of a common painkiller she sourced from a new supplier is putting people in Aurochs Medical Complex — she doesn't know yet, but the trail leads back to her stall
The girl she's been secretly funding shows up at her stall, having figured out who's been paying her fees, and now knows enough to destroy Adaora's reputation
narrative_function: Local color and information node; she hears everything from desperate people; can supply medical items, mild drugs, or rumors; potential quest giver when a regular customer goes missing
augmentations: Cosmetic iris mod (violet-to-copper shift); subdermal thermal regulators in her hands for precise compound preparation; no other chrome
daily_life: Rises before dawn to grind fresh compounds and restock her portable cooling units, then runs her stall from sunrise until two hours past dark, trading gossip and remedies in equal measure.
affiliation: Independent; pays protection to the Oxidian Market Vendors Guild; The Gauze

decision_rules: Never sell to anyone visibly in withdrawal without first asking what they already have in their system
Always keep one free remedy for anyone who genuinely cannot pay
Never give names to anyone who asks about customers
escalation_ladder: Becomes formal and clinical, creates distance
Quietly contacts Guild enforcers via wrist-tap message without breaking composure

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assesses them medically before socially — eyes their pupils, their gait, their skin
interpersonal_modes.friends: Feeds them, remembers their families' names, keeps their secrets like pressed flowers

stress_responses.medium: Goes very still and very precise
stress_responses.high: Retreats into full clinical detachment, stops using names, refers to people as 'the patient'

contradictions: Deeply ethical about honesty in all things except the one death that haunts her
Motherly and nurturing while also profiting from dependence
habits: Sniffs everything someone hands her before accepting it
Keeps a small wrapped bundle of herbs from her grandmother's village in her breast pocket at all times
Hums Igbo folk songs under her breath while grinding
breaking_points: Someone dying in front of her stall from something she sold them
Being directly asked by the dead boy's sister if she knew him

timeline.event: 2148 — Born in the Alban Souk district to a Igbo-Polish family of market traders
2168 — Apprenticed to a licensed herbalist who later lost their license in a Helix Biosystems patent enforcement sweep
2174 — Took over her mentor's pitch after the woman fled creditors
2197 — Pires Fonseca-Amadi dies; Adaora begins anonymous payments to his sister

physical_description.heritage: A striking genetic tapestry of the Ubiquitous Diaspora — Eastern European foundation (39.9%) providing strong bone structure and baseline complexion, substantially enriched by East Asian (19.9%) and Southeast Asian (17.7%) features creating distinctive facial geometry. Hispanic/Latin American (14.8%), Sub-Saharan African (5.9%), and Indigenous American (1.8%) ancestry layer warm golden and bronze undertones throughout. Her ancestry is written in her face: high Slavic cheekbones, monolid eye shapes from East Asian genetics, broader nose bridge and face width from Southeast Asian heritage, with warm saturated undertones from her Latin American and African heritage creating a sun-weathered bronze that shifts between olive and rich copper depending on light.
physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and sturdy, with the dense musculature of someone who has stood at a market stall for thirty years grinding compounds by hand. Not heavy, but solid — carries weight with authority rather than bulk.
physical_description.hair_color: Natural dark brown with silver threading at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Wrapped tightly and tucked beneath a wide-brimmed hat; when exposed, worn in neat locs past shoulder length
physical_description.eye_color: Warm brown iris with cosmetic shift-mod that cycles between deep violet and copper-gold depending on ambient light and angle
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm bronze-olive complexion with rich saturation — a harmonious blend of Eastern European paleness lifted by East Asian yellow undertones, Southeast Asian golden warmth, and deeper bronze notes from Sub-Saharan and Indigenous American heritage, creating a sun-weathered richness that speaks of decades outdoors across multiple climates
physical_description.complexion: Face creased from fifty-two years of outdoor work and genuine smiling; laugh lines around eyes are prominent. Skin is clear but textured, with faint burn scars on her cheekbones from a market fire in her thirties. Her features blend Slavic high cheekbones with East Asian monolid eye shapes and Southeast Asian nose bridge — a striking asymmetrical beauty reflecting her diverse genetic inheritance, warmed throughout by deep bronze undertones from her Latin American, Sub-Saharan, and Indigenous American heritage.
distinguishing_marks: Pale burn scar tissue runs across both cheekbones in a starburst pattern, legacy of a propane fire at the Souk in 1998
Deep indigo tattoo on her left inner forearm: an Adinkra symbol (Sankofa) inked by a street artist twenty years ago
Chronic dark staining on her palms and fingers from botanical compounds — pigment embedded so deeply it's nearly permanent despite daily scrubbing
Small raised scar on her right temple where an early-model iris mod was crudely installed
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Cosmetic shift-iris mod visible in her warm brown eyes (the violet-copper cycling is unmistakable under direct light). Subdermal thermal regulators in her hands are not externally visible but her palms maintain a steady warmth even in cold weather — observant people notice she never shivers. Her hands move with unnatural precision and steadiness when working.
physical_description.posture_movement: She stands rooted at her stall like a tree — weight evenly distributed, shoulders back, head slightly forward as if always listening. Her movements are economical and deliberate; she doesn't fidget or waste motion. When she walks, she moves slowly but with purpose, her broad frame parting crowds without aggression. Her hands are always moving: grinding, measuring, reaching, gesturing. She speaks with her whole body.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 practical wear layered for all weather. A loose linen shirt (faded indigo, handwashed) tucked into wide canvas trousers with multiple pockets and reinforced seams. Over this, a heavy canvas apron stained with decades of botanical residue — reds, yellows, browns, blacks. Her wide-brimmed plastene hat (cream-colored, weathered to gray-tan) is strung with dried medicinal herbs, prayer beads, and small glass vials of her most popular compounds. She wears a heavy cloth wrap — currently rust-colored — tied loosely around her shoulders. Her shoes are practical market boots, scuffed and resoled multiple times. No jewelry except for a single silver ring on her right ring finger, unmarked. Everything about her dress screams 'I am here to work, not to impress.'
